title: Realtime multiplexing kernel-slice allocator: prefill vs decode overlap draft
body:
Context

This is a working draft proposing a realtime multiplexing approach plus a light-weight kernel-slice allocator to better overlap prefill work and autoregressive decode in our serving runtime. Goal is to reduce tail latency for short streaming sessions while preserving throughput for long-running decodes and keeping KV cache residency bounded.

Problem statement
- Prefill (encoder-like work for context) and decode (autoregressive emission) are currently scheduled in disjoint phases in many slots. That leads to hard serialization for mixed workloads: short queries wait behind large prefill batches, long chats suffer jitter as we switch priorities.
- Existing microbatching heuristics favor throughput but hurt 95/99th percentile latency for interactive streams.
- KV cache residency grows unbounded when many partial prefill results are retained long enough for decode to resume, leading to memory pressure and eviction churn.

Design goals
1) Allow safe overlap of prefill and decode on GPUs where kernels do not interfere (memory-aware).
2) Provide per-stream priority lanes so interactive streams get progressive decoding with minimal prefill blocking.
3) Keep microbatching benefits for throughput while bounding single-request added latency.
4) Maintain determinism for cache contents and the ability to fall back to non-overlapped execution if kernel conflicts are detected.
5) Operational visibility: track slot-level state, prefill KV epochs, and eviction intents.

Key concepts introduced
- kernel-slice: a minimal unit of kernel work sized to fit within a scheduling quantum. Examples: a single attention kernel invocation for N tokens, or a small GEMM slice. The allocator maps kernel-slices onto GPU timeslices.
- slice-allocator: component that assigns kernel-slices to execution lanes based on priority, memory footprint, and KV residency constraints.
- lane: abstraction for priority buckets. At minimum: realtime (low-latency interactive), steady (throughput-oriented), background (batch/eviction tasks).
- prefill-epoch: a monotonic counter per request representing the prefill progress that decoders reference for KV validity.

High-level flow
1) Ingress: requests are classified into lanes by SLA, input-length, and historical token rate. Short interactive queries are mapped to realtime lane.
2) Prefill generation: prefill work is split into kernel-slices. Early critical slices (e.g., last n tokens for attention context) are marked hot and prioritized for realtime lanes. Bulk prefill slices are lower priority.
3) Slice allocation: slice-allocator maintains a queue per lane, with a per-lane allowed GPU timeshare. It picks slices respecting these shares and kernel anti-affinity rules.
4) Decode emission: when a stream is eligible to decode and its prefill-epoch is at least the minimum required, decode kernels can run concurrently in separate lanes if memory permits. If not, decode waits or runs a reduced kernel variant.
5) KV lifecycle: KV entries are tagged with prefill-epoch and lane origin. Eviction policies consider both age and lane priority; realtime-lane KV is kept longer but compacted more aggressively (quantized) when hardware allows.

Allocator heuristics and constraints
- Memory check before dispatch: estimate transient workspace + KV working set for the slice. If combined required memory exceeds a safe threshold, do not overlap; either stall or schedule a compact kernel variant.
- Kernel affinity table: precomputed compatibility map for kernel pairs that can run concurrently on same GPU without causing bank conflicts or catastrophic throughput drops. Populated with microbenchmarks per architecture.
- Timeshare quotas: realtime lane gets small high-frequency slices to keep tail latency down; steady lane gets larger aggregated slices to maximize throughput efficiency. Example default: realtime 10% GPU time, steady 80%, background 10%. Tunable per tenant.
- Slice coalescing: small adjacent slices from the same request may be coalesced when tenant throughput allows, preventing too many tiny kernel launches. Coalescing respects latency budgets of the originating lane.

Priority and fairness
- Weighted round-robin across lanes with urgent preemption: if realtime queue grows beyond threshold, preemption tokens are used to interrupt steady work at safe boundaries and reopen capacity for small realtime slices.
- Admission control: reject or queue new long prefill requests into steady lane when realtime backlog exceeds SLO thresholds.
- Slow-start for new long-lived sessions: start in realtime lane for the first few short responses, then migrate to steady if the session indicates sustained high token rates.

KV cache management
- KV epoching: every prefill increases the request's prefill-epoch. Decoders only reference KV entries with epoch == current or epoch == current - 1 depending on safe handoff policy. This avoids reading partially-overlapped cache states.
- Compacting hot KV: for realtime-lane KV entries we maintain a compacted representation (lower precision or hashed keys) to reduce residency. Compaction is applied asynchronously in background lane when GPU idle pockets are detected.
- Eviction hints: slice-allocator emits eviction hints when it predicts eviction pressure, enabling opportunistic persistence to CPU or compressed storage.

Fallbacks and safety nets
- Conservative fallback: if memory estimator or kernel-affinity map returns unknown, allocator falls back to non-overlapping execution for that slot.
- Deterministic replay mode: for debugging or audits, we can force strict prefill->decode serial ordering to reproduce behavior. This is expensive but useful for root-cause.

Pseudo-algorithm (simplified)
- on_request(req):
    lane = classify(req)
    prefill_slices = split_prefill(req.input)
    for slice in prefill_slices:
      enqueue(slice, lane)

- slice_dispatch_loop():
    while true:
      lane = pick_lane_by_quota()   # weighted RR with preemption availability
      slice = lane.dequeue_next_ready()
      if memory_ok(slice) and affinity_ok(slice, running_set):
         launch(slice)
      else if lane == realtime and can_preempt():
         preempt_running_noncritical()
         launch(slice)
      else:
         if slice.size < coalesce_threshold:
            coalesce_with_next(slice)
         else:
            sleep_short_backoff()

Operational instrumentation and metrics to add
- per-lane GPU time share (percent) and effective latency percentiles
- kernel-affinity conflict counter and episodes where fallback occurred
- KV occupancy by lane and by prefill-epoch histogram
- number of preemptions and preemption latency cost
- microbatch size distribution per lane

Experiments to run (prioritization)
1) Microbench kernel affinity matrix: run pairwise kernel runs across our GPU fleet to identify safe co-runs and quantify throughput loss.
2) Small-slice vs large-slice tradeoff: measure 95/99 p latency for short interactive workloads while varying slice size and realtime timeshare.
3) KV compaction benefit: simulate workload mix and test compacted KV representation impact on eviction rate and latency.
4) Preemption overhead: instrument cost of preempting steady work for realtime arrival and tune safe preemption points.

Open questions and tradeoffs
- How aggressive should KV compaction be for realtime lanes? Heavy compaction saves memory but may reduce generation fidelity for follow-ups. Need evaluator runs to measure quality impact.
- Where to place the boundary for safe kernel co-runs? Conservative approach reduces wins; aggressive may cause subtle throughput cliffs on some architectures.
- Multi-tenant fairness: should realtime timeshare be tenant-configurable or enforced by global policy? Tenant-configurable improves SLAs but risks noise for others.

Implementation notes and next steps
- Short-term: implement slice-allocator prototype in Python scheduler with a limited kernel-affinity table and conservative memory checks. Add telemetry hooks.
- Mid-term: migrate allocator into C++ runtime, expose per-tenant timeshare config via control-plane, and integrate KV compaction workers.
- Long-term: auto-tune slice sizes and lane quotas using production telemetry and an offline optimizer in Optimize product.

TODO
- [ ] Create kernel microbench harness and run affinity experiments (owner: Daniel)
- [ ] Add telemetry events for prefill-epoch lifecycle (owner: Marta)
- [ ] Prototype slice-allocator and run mixed workload sim (owner: Luis)
- [ ] Draft API for per-tenant lane overrides and safe defaults (owner: Aisha)

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally exploratory. Looking for feedback on heuristics, missing safety checks, and whether the lane quotas should be global or per-GPU.
- If you add benchmark links or kernel numbers, please append to linked_artifacts.
